cycle.name: Strength + Aerobic Base
cycle.why: Nine weeks, Monday to Friday: test, three Base weeks, two Build weeks, a primer/deload week, a retest week and a flex week. Week 1 tests a 3RM back squat and deadlift, a 5RM strict press and a 1 km run (or 1,000 m row); every lift percentage comes from estimated max (3RM × 1.06, press 5RM × 1.13) with an RPE 8 cap, and every run pace comes from the 1 km time. Monday and Friday are the hard days, Wednesday is steady threshold work, Thursday is easy, the lift always comes before conditioning, and class running rises no more than 10% a week. Stations live in Wednesday conditioning, compromised running starts in Week 5, and toes-to-bar is the block skill (baseline Week 2, retest Week 9). Week 8 repeats the Week 1 tests on the same days, and the Week 8 numbers plus the Week 9 Helen, Mini Challenge and strict pull-up baselines become the next block's starting points.
goals: Raise 3RM back squat and deadlift and 5RM strict press
Faster 1 km run or 1,000 m row
Learn the stations and running off them

1.notes: Heavy back squat, then short bike or row intervals. No running on squat day.

2.notes: Toes-to-bar skill block, then the week's main aerobic running. 1 km test and retest live here (Wk 1 and 8).

3.notes: Deadlift, then threshold work at about 7/10 on stations; compromised running in Weeks 5–6.

4.notes: Easy day: accessory supersets and core, then easy row/bike intervals with set work and rest.

5.notes: Power clean technique, then strict press, then a short hard workout. Cindy Wk 4, Mini Challenge Wk 9.

workouts.title: Squat Test + Bike/Row Intervals
workouts.why: Find the most you can squat for 3 good reps. It sets your squat weights for the next few weeks. Then short, fast intervals to open up the lungs.
workouts.coach_notes:
Two coaches on test days if possible. Watch depth and back position; you call the set. Every level tests the barbell back squat (smaller jumps at Steady). Machine-only intervals: Monday has no running on purpose (heavy-leg day), so no outside version.
Scaling: easier warm-up: step instead of jump, walk instead of jog, comfortable range. Newer lifters / first 4 weeks after on-ramp: start with the empty bar (or lighter training bar), no max attempt; stop at the first RPE 8 set and record that. Masters (40+): RPE 8 max on the interval hard pieces. Knee or back pain: air bike only.
Test: stop at RPE 8 (2 reps left), no RPE 9–10 grinders. Record load in lb, level, coach notes. Week 1 3RM × 1.06 = e1RM for every squat % this block.
Intervals: hard pieces Steady RPE 7, Strong RPE 8, Full RPE 9. Same machine all 6 rounds. Cap 12:00 (fixed) · Aim: hold calories within 10% from round 1 to round 6 · Feel: gas · Pace: reach. No machine: score = reps instead of calories.
No machine (warm-up/cool-down): easy jumping jacks, marching or jump rope, about 1:00 per 250 m or per 5 cal.

workouts.title: 1 km Test + Toes-to-Bar
workouts.why: Our one run test: your 1 km time sets your run and row paces for the next few weeks. Toes-to-bar work stays light today.
workouts.coach_notes:
Start the 1 km in waves of 4–6 and read times out as they finish; if rowers run out inside, the next wave rows when a machine frees up (don't swap the test). Members choose run or row once and repeat the same option in Week 8. The easy flush needs no machines inside (jump ropes, floor space), so finished waves start it while the next wave rows. Write each member's time on their scorecard; it sets all run paces (easy = +1:30–2:30/km, threshold = +0:40–0:50/km).
Scaling: easier warm-up: step instead of jump, walk instead of jog, comfortable range.
Test targets: Cap 15:00 · Feel: cardio · Pace: reach. Row aim: even 500 m splits. Run aim: Steady 5:45–8:00 (jog/walk is fine), Strong 4:45–5:45, Full 3:45–4:45. Anyone who jogs and walks keeps the same plan in Week 8. No machine: next free rower, or the 1 km run outside if safe; a bodyweight swap can't be compared with Week 8.
Flush: RPE 5. Cap 12:00 · Aim: smooth and easy · Feel: cardio (easy) · Pace: sustain.

workouts.title: "Easy" Recovery
workouts.why: Thursday is the easy day, so the accessories and core stay as planned. The Row/Bike Fives are swapped for an Easy Ladder that changes tool every interval, for more variety without more effort.
workouts.coach_notes:
Coach notes

The point: it's an easy aerobic day with some movement mixed in, not a test. Everyone should be able to talk in short sentences the whole time. If someone can only manage a word or two, slow them down.
EMOM pace: the swings and step-ups should take about 35–45 seconds, leaving 15–25 seconds of easy rest. If someone needs the whole minute, drop their weight or reps.
Machines: start half the class on the row and half on the bike so nobody waits, then flip. If there aren't enough machines, swap a 2:00 piece for 2:00 of easy jumping jacks or a jog outside.
Swings: hips drive the bell, the arms just guide it, and it stops at chest height. Anyone with a sore back does KB deadlifts, Gentle style.
Step-ups: step all the way up and stand tall, alternating legs. No jumping, since it's a recovery day.
Masters and anyone sore: use a lower box and stay at RPE 5.
Scoring: nothing to record. If you want something for members, have them aim for the same row split and the same bike pace on both bouts.

workouts.title: Light Deadlift + Helen

No machine free (inside): Steady 125 jumping jacks, Strong/Full 250 single-unders in place of the row (not comparable).

workouts.title: Light Press + Mini Challenge
workouts.why: Our Mini Challenge: 4 short runs or bike legs, each followed by a station. Your time is the baseline for the next block.
workouts.coach_notes:
Flex week: every session is optional (members pick 3–4); guests and on-ramp members join at Steady. Two coaches if possible. Run heats of 4 (one rower each) starting every 3:00. Members count their own reps; the coach records total time and the first and last run (or bike) splits on the scorecard. Benchmark: Full is the Rx standard so scores compare with the published version; every member records their level.
Strength: optional technique work, smooth reps, rest 90 s. Not a test.
Steady lunges: 13/22 lb sandbag optional.
Challenge targets: Cap 26:00 · Aim: Steady finish under the cap, Strong 17:00–23:00, Full 15:00–20:00 · Feel cardio · Pace sustain (even run or bike splits). Lighter option: drop to Steady at RPE 6.
No machine free (inside): Steady 75 jumping jacks for the row, 70 for each bike; Strong/Full 250 single-unders for the row, 140 for each bike. Note the swap on the scorecard.
Scaling: Masters (40+) never above 85%, RPE 8 is the ceiling. Newer lifters / first 4 weeks: same sets with empty bar or light plates at RPE 7. Pain: pain-free range, tell the coach.
